newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Cotton prices likely down in India, up in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Cotton prices likely down in India, up in Pakistan.

text.p: Pakistani cotton prices are likely to edge up on rising demand next week, while new crop arrivals in India are expected to depress prices, dealers said on Thursday.
Karachi dealers said prices remained mixed to weak this week, with spinners on the sidelines amid reports that ginners were holding back stocks of more than a million bales.

The state Cotton Export Corporation of Pakistan said on Sunday that the 1996/97 (July-June) crop had reached a provisional 3.464 million 375-lb bales by November 7, up from 2.499 million bales in the same period last year.
It said a total of 1.079 million unsold bales were stocked at ginning factories, up from 722,100 in the year-ago period.

"Some major spinners halted buying to bring the prices down," dealer Nasim Usman said. But ginners resisted the move and most spinners were likely get back in the market to meet their immediate requirements, he said.

Dealers said the crop was smaller than last year's and if spinners did not buy their requirements now, when supplies are plentiful, they might have to pay higher prices later. Officials say this year's cotton crop is now expected to reach 9.2 to 9.5 million bales, down from a target of 10 million bales and the 1995/96 crop of 9.96 million bales.
The private Karachi Cotton Association's (KCA) spot rates were steady on Thursday amid selective buying by spinners.
In the kerb market NIAB-78 traded at 2,300 rupees ($57.18) per maund (37.32 kg), dealers said.

Indian cotton prices fell in Bombay this week on low mill demand and quiet sentiment, amid limited fresh arrivals, traders said. "New crop arrivals remained low due to the Diwali festival, but they will pick up up next week," one dealer said.

In spot deals Bengal-deshi fell to 915/940 rupees per maund from 920/960 rupees while Punjab saw-ginned fell to 1,590/1,680 rupees per maund from 1,600/1,750 rupees. Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) moved down to 18,800/19,800 per candy (355.56 kg) from 19,000/20,500 rupees.
Demand from cash-strapped millers was low and volume was thin in the run-up to next week's Cotton Advisory Board meeting.

"New crop for cotton year 1996/97 (October-September) is estimated at 16 million (170-kg) bales. The Cotton Advisory Board may come out with the same figure next week," said Chandulal Thakkar, a leading dealer.

"There will be some crop loss in Gujarat and southern India due to the recent cyclone and unseasonal rain but higher yield per hectare will balance this," he said, estimating yield per hectare at 300 kg.

"Meanwhile the Indian government has allowed export of 15,000 tonnes of cotton yarn for November. This move will enhance export of cotton yarn and in turn will ease the monetary crunch faced by the millers," he said.
